subject: Biology
title: Marine Snow: Food from Above
description: A quick, practical guide to Marine Snow: Food from Above.

hook.text: In the deep ocean, there's no sunlight and no plants. All food comes from above—falling like snow.

buildup.text: Marine snow is a constant shower of dead plankton, fecal matter, and organic debris from the surface.

discovery.text: It takes weeks for a particle to sink from the surface to the abyssal floor, thousands of meters below.

twist.text: Whale falls—dead whales sinking to the bottom—create entire ecosystems that can last for decades.

climax.text: Deep-sea life depends entirely on this slow rain of death from above. No snow, no life.

punchline.text: In the deep, dinner is whatever drifts down from the surface.

quiz.question: What is marine snow?
options: Dead organic matter falling from the surface to the deep ocean
Frozen seawater crystals at the poles

details.summary: Marine snow is the continuous shower of organic particles, dead plankton, fecal pellets, and mucus, that sinks from surface waters to the deep ocean. This biological fallout is the primary food source for most deep-sea life and plays a crucial role in the ocean carbon cycle.
details.whyItMatters: Marine snow transfers carbon from the atmosphere to the deep ocean, a process called the biological pump. This mechanism removes billions of tons of CO2 from the surface each year, making it vital for climate regulation.
takeaways: Marine snow is the main food source for organisms in the deep ocean
Only about 1 to 3 percent of surface production reaches the deep seafloor
The biological pump sequesters atmospheric carbon in the deep ocean for centuries

faq.question: What is marine snow made of?
faq.answer: It consists of dead phytoplankton and zooplankton, fecal pellets, mucous feeding structures, and mineral particles that aggregate into larger clumps as they sink. These fragile particles are consumed and repackaged by organisms at every depth as they descend.

faq.question: How does marine snow affect climate?
faq.answer: By transporting carbon fixed by photosynthesis at the surface to the deep ocean, marine snow removes CO2 from contact with the atmosphere for centuries to millennia. This biological pump is essential for regulating atmospheric CO2 and mitigating climate change.
